13.PRE – MALIGNANT LESION OF VULVA:
•Patch testing in dermatosis.
•Serum ferritin in Dermatosis.
•Biopsy when diagnosis not clear clinically or suspicion of VIN.

Benign vulva lesions:

lesion

Features

Treatment and follow up

Lichen sclerosis

SCC= <5%

  • -Autoimmune HLA DQ – 7.
  • -Cigarette paper, white shiny appearance
  • -Tissue paper, figure of 8 appearance

Histopathology: hyalinization, no vaginal involvement

Auto antibodies against Extra cellular matrix protein.

  • -Ultra potent steroid.
  • -Daily for 1m0.
  • -Alternate days for nesxt2ndm0.
  • -Twice weekly for next3rd m0.

F/U – at 3m0 then at 1year at vulval clinic. Afterwards yearly lifelong with GP

Lichen planus

Erosive – most common

MDT: vulval clinic SSC – 3%.

  • -Autoimmune in erosive type.

5Ps for characteristic lesions:

  • -Polygonal, purple, pruritic, plaque, planner
  • -Wickham stria
  • - T – cell immunity
  • -Involvement of vaginal/oral mucosa.

H/P: saw tooth Appearance acanthosis, band like dermal infiltrates.

  • -Ultra-potent steroids.
  • -Vaginal steroid
  • -hydrocortisone with applicators at sensitive areas and mild disease.

Lichen Simplex

  • -Thickened pale, scaly, leathery skin.
  • -Involvement of thigh, pubic hair often lost @ site of itching.

H/P: Epithelial thickening, mitosis in Basel and prickle layers.

  • -Emollient soap.
  • -Topical steroids.

Paget’s disease.

  • -Red, pink, crusty, white cake icing effect, strawberry cream effect, velvety texture, islands of keratosis.

H/P: rounded, atypical cells with oval nuclei, pale cytoplasm.

  • -Wide load excision.
  • -2 weeks referral pathway
  • -Examination of breast, Anus.

F/U: Anal, vulva extension and breast examination 3m0 for 2 years then annually.

Vulval Crohn’s

  • -Swollen, edematous, granules, abscesses and draining sinuses.

Bechet’s Disease.

  • -Recurrent oral, genital ulcers painful with scaring

Pemphigoid

  • -Older women, subdermal blisters.
  • -Healing with scaring.

Immunofluorescence:

  • -Antibodies deposits at dermo-epidermal junction.

Pemphigus

  • -Younger women
  • -Intradermal blisters.
  • -Healing without scaring.

Immunofluorescence:

  • -Antibodies deposits @ intra dermal layer of epidermis.

Vulvodynia

  • -Generalized
  • -Localized
  • ⇨Vestibulodynia
  • ⇨Clitorodynia
  • ⇨Hemivulodynia.
  • -Provoked or unprovoked

Provoked with intercourse, Tampon use, light touch.

  • -Education.
  • -Rule out organic cause
  • -Rule out psychological trauma like sexual abuse
  • -Vulval care
  • -2 or 5% lidocaine 30 min before intercourse
  • -Iintra lesion therapy
  • -Botox injection
  • -TCA – SSRI – SNRI.
  • -Antipsycotics.
  • -Psychological counselling
  • -Psychosexual counselling

Table 10. Benign vulva lesions

Benign Valval Diseases VIN:

Unusual VIN (Basaloid)

•Common, warty.
•Young women 35 – 55 years
•Association with HPV – 16.
•Less risk of cancer = 10%
•Multifocal Multicentric lesions
•Warty/Basaloid SSC.
•Medical treatment more effective.

Differentiated VIN:

•Less common.
•Old women 55 – 85 years.
•Associated with Lichen sclerosis and Lichen Planus.
•Unifocal lesions, ulcers, plaque.
•Keratinizing SCC.
•50% risk of CA.
•Surgical treatment more effective.

 

Treatment of VIN:

•Counselling regarding life style.
•Imiquimod 5%.
•5 fluorouracil cream.
•Local destruction by laser
•Local excision
•Vulvectomy.

Before surgery for VIN:

-Colposcopy
-Vulvoscopy.

-Vaginoscopy.

Recurrence: 26%

F/U:

•6monthly for 2 years
•Annually for 5 years.
•Guidance regarding self-examination

 

Imiquimod:

•S/E redness, itching, soreness, fluelike symptoms.
•same success as surgery @ 6months of use
